# Review of the OIDC step-up session-expiry change

**Verdict: fix one thing before opening the PR.** A step-up now accepts any valid session cookie as "the session to elevate." It doesn't check whose session it is or which login method created it.

This was a range review of committed work only: 4 files, +286 −5, base `e36e81e` → head `0acc291`, 3 commits. No files were changed, no tests were run and nothing was posted.

## What held the review back

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Security | 1 confirmed problem (priority P1): the step-up isn't tied to the person it elevates |
| Testing | 1 gap (P2): no test covers a prior cookie from another user or from a wallet (SIWE) login |
| Bugs, regression, architecture, performance, DRY, conventions | Nothing found |
| KISS | 1 nit (P3): the same rationale is written out in three comments |

Only the security finding went through the paired prove/disprove check (1 of 3 findings). Both agents agreed it holds. The other two are my own judgement and weren't independently checked. I read all nine areas myself in one pass rather than running one reviewer per area, because the change is small. I didn't produce a number score because two of the three findings are unchecked, and a number would look more rigorous than the review was.

## Fix before opening

**1. A step-up accepts any valid session cookie, from any user or login method** (P1, confirmed)
`src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.service.ts:237`

- **What:** `getPriorExpiration` checks the cookie's signature, then keeps only its `.exp`. It never checks that `auth_method === 'oidc'`, and never checks that `sub` equals the `userId` returned by `findOrCreateByExtUserIdAndEmail` (`:156`).
- **Why it matters:** The comment at `:188-191` says the new rejection stops a step-up from acting as a login based only on Auth0's SSO session. But `GET /v1/auth/oidc/authorize?elevate=true` needs no login (`oidc-auth.controller.ts:114`), and the cookie comes straight from the request (`oidc-auth.controller.ts:238`). So:
  1. A throwaway wallet (SIWE) login gives the browser a valid cookie.
  2. The browser starts a step-up and completes Auth0 plus MFA as a different account.
  3. The callback mints an elevated token for that account, with a fresh `mfa_verified_at` and the throwaway session's expiry. That token then passes `ElevationGuard` (`src/routes/common/auth/elevation.guard.ts:56-83`).
- **Limits:** This is not an account takeover. The attacker still has to pass Auth0 and MFA for the account they elevate. What fails is the "you must already be logged in as this user" check this change adds.
- **Fix:** Have `getPriorExpiration` return the decoded payload. Then reject the step-up unless `auth_method === AuthMethod.Oidc` and `sub === userId.toString()`. That comparison needs the `userId`, so resolve it before the expiry decision (or do the check after `findOrCreate…` and before `signToken`).
- **Checked by:** the validator (CONFIRMED, impact I3, likelihood L3) and the refuter (STANDS). The refuter confirmed that the OIDC `state` has no user binding (`oidc-state.entity.ts:4-14`) and the rate-limit guard does no identity check.

## Worth a ticket or a quick change

| # | Priority | Where | What | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | P2 | `src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.service.spec.ts:505` | Every "session lifetime on step-up" test mocks `decodeToken` with `oidcAuthPayloadDtoBuilder()` and a `sub` that is never compared. Nothing would catch finding 1. | Add a test with a `sub` that doesn't match, and one with a SIWE payload (`siweAuthPayloadDtoBuilder`, if the repo has one). Both should expect `UnauthorizedException` and no `signToken` call. |
| 3 | P3 | `src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.service.ts:223-230` | The "absolute timeout, step-up must not reset the clock" rationale appears in the `@param` doc (`:91-94`), in `getSessionExpiration` (`:183-191`) and again in `getPriorExpiration`. | Keep it once, in `getSessionExpiration`, and trim the `getPriorExpiration` doc to what it returns. |

## What held up

- `decodeToken` verifies the signature and the expiry (`jwt.module.ts:53-72`). A tampered or expired cookie is rejected, and the error is logged at debug level without the token.
- The expiry is decided before `findOrCreateByExtUserIdAndEmail` runs, so a rejected step-up doesn't create a user.
- The prior expiry is still capped at `maxExpirationTime`.
- In production the session cookie is `SameSite=Lax` (`auth-cookie.utils.ts:20`), so the browser does send it on Auth0's top-level redirect back to the callback. The cookie will reach the callback.
- The injected `LoggingService` follows the repo's `@Inject(LoggingService) private readonly` pattern, and all three places in the spec that build the service were updated.
- `authenticateWithOidc` has only one caller (`oidc-auth.controller.ts:235`).

## Not checked

- I didn't run tests, lint or type-check, as instructed.
- Findings 2 and 3 didn't get the paired check.
- There were no cleanup proposals, because the only follow-ups are the findings above.
- There was no earlier run to compare against.
